newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Zaldivar copper mine cuts 96 output goal.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Zaldivar copper mine cuts 96 output goal.

text.p: The Zaldivar copper mine in northern Chile has cut its production target this year to 75,000 tonnes from 85,000 tonnes as originally planned as the result of lower-than-expected copper recovery levels, said an official.
Production has been hurt by higher than anticipated levels of fine copper-rich mineral in the oxide deposit, said the mine's public relations manager Mario Illanes.
This material is too fine be processed through the heapleach system and is having to be deposited as waste in tailings dumps, Illanes told Reuters.
"More than originally expected amounts of copper in tailings is perhaps the biggest single reason for this level of production," he said.
Despite the lower output this year, the pit expects to hit design capacity of 125,000 tonnes on schedule in 1997, he said.
Owned equally by Finland's Outokumpu Oy and Canadian gold producer Placer Dome, Zaldivar cast its first copper cathode last year.
The pit suffered a slow startup as the result of technical glitches with output last year of around 25,000 tonnes against a target of 40,000 tonnes.
The mine has mineral reserves of 425 million tonnes and is expected to have an operating life of 19 years.
